Dear Friends,
This week, I am releasing an episode where I was joined by my lovely and brave young friend, Chole Cole. I absolutely adore her. Chloe was one of the first *child* detransitioners and spoke out about her regrets and all of the apparatus that pushed her into making this life-altering decision. Unfortunately, from my experience, the trans-train is a ride a child can rarely get off of once they get on.
Since her decision to live according to her DNA (i.e., XX chromosome), Chloe has been the target of radical left-wing groups who vehemently protest her venues all across the country as she educates people about her experience and the lack of ethics in this growing and LUCRATIVE industry.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/f581d6a7-7d7f-465a-a166-284e02d4157f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I'm not a doctor and I don't attempt to pretend to be one in this interview. I'm a mom. I love my own children and I want to protect all others. This is a very important topic to all of us...whether you know that or not.
LISTEN. SUBSCRIBE. SHARE IT.

subject: Jamie Dimon agrees with this, do you?

body:
| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=1846%2E4032634%2E98itAD)
---
When it comes to banking policy, I don’t usually find myself agreeing with the CEOs of multi-billion-dollar banks. Wednesday was an exception. The heads of some of America’s biggest banks — we’re talking JP Morgan, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, and so on — came before the Senate Banking Committee. I asked them whether the same anti-money-laundering rules they have to follow should also apply to crypto. Right down the line, they all said “absolutely.” Jamie Dimon threw in a “positively” and a “certainly” for good measure. That was a nice touch. The fact that big bank CEOs and I are all on the same page on this one just goes to show how glaring of a problem we’re facing. It’s a matter of fairness, but it’s also a matter of national security. Criminals use crypto to finance terrorists, drug traffickers, and sanctioned countries, like Russia and Iran and North Korea. They couldn’t use regular banks, because regular banks are required to have systems in place to track and shut down those transactions. But crypto’s loopholes let them stay in the shadows, trading billions of dollars with complete anonymity. Crypto firms should have to follow the same anti-money-laundering standards as banks, stockbrokers, credit card companies, Venmo, Western Union, and all other financial institutions. **And I’ve got a bipartisan bill for that: the Digital Asset Anti-Money Laundering Act. It is the toughest proposal on the table to crack down on crypto crime and give regulators the tools they need to stop the flow of crypto to bad actors.** But crypto lobbyists are working overtime to block reform. They claim crypto is special. So special that they deserve special exceptions from basic rules of the road. They claim they shouldn’t have to comply with standard regulations, even if that means letting terrorists, drug traffickers, ransomware criminals, rogue nations move billions of dollars totally unrestricted. [**Crypto doesn’t get a pass to help the world’s worst criminals, no matter how special they think they are. To pass this bill, Washington needs to hear that the American people are calling for change. Please add your name to say you support making crypto firms follow the same anti-money-laundering rules as banks. Jamie Dimon agrees — do you?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-crypto-regulation/?source=EMZ18A_BAN_E_20231208_V1S1&t=8&akid=1846%2E4032634%2E98itAD) Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth

body:
| | | | | [](https://us.engagingnetworks.app/page/email/click/10012/2184532?email=RepJ2ZGQKX6xm5Aey7FwClESkN1MQhKC&campid=UI6tX83ZqbKZkArzVWMSmA==)
---|---|---

| | **URGENT PLASTIC PETITON: Plastic is destroying our oceans, invading our bodies, and threatening the future of our planet.**[_**Tell the Biden Administration to take bold action immediately >>**_](https://us.engagingnetworks.app/page/email/click/10012/2184533?email=RepJ2ZGQKX6xm5Aey7FwClESkN1MQhKC&campid=UI6tX83ZqbKZkArzVWMSmA==)** ** _**Every piece of plastic threatens the future of our oceans and planet:** _
* Plastic debris _CHOKES_ and KILLS **OVER A MILLION marine species every year,** like baby sea turtles and dolphins.
* Plastic is _**NON-BIODEGRADABLE**_ which means the plastic that was discarded in our communities and oceans many years ago will _**NEVER DISAPPEAR.**_
* Plastic breaks down and becomes **_microplastics_** which contaminates our food, water, and air supply.
* Massive plastic facilities **spew toxic pollutants into nearby communities of color,** increasing the risk of serious health conditions for nearby residents.

**The impact is clear, Friend.** If the U.S. government does not enact immediate federal solutions, we may lose our one and only planet to plastic. Big Plastic and Big Oil is counting on our inaction to fuel their dirty practices and fill their pockets. But we know environmentalists like YOU will not stand for corporate greed. [_**Sign the petition NOW to demand the Biden Administration take crucial action against plastic production and pollution >>**_](https://us.engagingnetworks.app/page/email/click/10012/2184534?email=RepJ2ZGQKX6xm5Aey7FwClESkN1MQhKC&campid=UI6tX83ZqbKZkArzVWMSmA==) | [SIGN THE PETITION](https://us.engagingnetworks.app/page/email/click/10012/2184535?email=RepJ2ZGQKX6xm5Aey7FwClESkN1MQhKC&campid=UI6tX83ZqbKZkArzVWMSmA==)
---
Greedy plastic corporations are placing profit over the planet and human health. It’s not just the actual plastic that is harmful but also the process it takes to produce it. Plastic manufacturing facilities burn through huge amounts of fossil fuels and release massive amounts of pollution. This exacerbates the climate crisis and puts nearby communities -- primarily communities of color and low-income communities -- at significantly higher risk of cancer and other serious illnesses.
Despite the dangers that come with plastic production, consumption, and pollution, Big Plastic and Big Oil have been steadily bumping production to a staggering 9% increase every year. Yet**less than 6%** of plastics are recycled annually in the United States.
**_We must act NOW to STOP this PLASTIC APOCALYPSE._** [_**Please, Friend, take action before our 11:59pm deadline TONIGHT to protect our health, our wildlife and the future of our planet.**_ ](https://us.engagingnetworks.app/page/email/click/10012/2184536?email=RepJ2ZGQKX6xm5Aey7FwClESkN1MQhKC&campid=UI6tX83ZqbKZkArzVWMSmA==)

It’s easy to chuckle at this photo — and see just how far fashion has changed since that classic _absolutely righteous_ 1970s bowtie — but it is also an opportunity to tell you about my upbringing. My family moved around while I was in school before settling in Danville, California. My parents and my teachers cultivated in me a love of and respect for public service. While in speech class, I remember listening to recordings of great speakers like President John F. Kennedy, the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr., and Winston Churchill. I admired the way they used language — how they could inspire millions of people to take action through the power of their words. I wanted to use words — and actions — in the service of progressive change. And I wanted to be part of the great struggle for the future. After graduating high school (I was not valedictorian as some have claimed — my B in Band held me back), I went on to college and law school. There, I learned how to gather the facts and argue my case. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/74831041/442775221/-613118499?refcode=AU_JC_FR_TAN_GEN_AC30_20231208_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84ODUyMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhODYyZDViZC0wYzk2LWVlMTEtODkyNS0wMDIyNDgyMjNmMzYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=F7IR7iyseFjDt3qtqbkD29fH1q-1pUxvJyq7OIoKDf8=) After law school, I was inspired by friends serving in office and decided I was ready to try. I ran for the California Assembly. And, folks, I lost. It was bruising to lose, but I didn’t give up. And then, I lost again. But I refused to give up hope. I continued campaigning and rallying — and just two years later, I was elected to represent the 21st District in the State Senate. I was sworn in as the California Senate’s youngest member at just 36 years old. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/74831042/442775222/-613118499?refcode=AU_JC_FR_TAN_GEN_AC30_20231208_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84ODUyMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhODYyZDViZC0wYzk2LWVlMTEtODkyNS0wMDIyNDgyMjNmMzYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=F7IR7iyseFjDt3qtqbkD29fH1q-1pUxvJyq7OIoKDf8=) After the term finished, I threw my hat in the ring to take on the Republican incumbent in California’s 27th congressional district. This was seen as one of the seats that could decide the House majority. Money poured into this election — the most expensive in history at the time. I barnstormed the district — speaking with voters to share our message. Those long months of hard work paid off: Despite the election of George W. Bush as president and Republicans maintaining their House majority, we flipped that seat and won that race, and I became only the second Democrat to represent the district in history. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/74831043/442775223/-613118499?refcode=AU_JC_FR_TAN_GEN_AC30_20231208_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84ODUyMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhODYyZDViZC0wYzk2LWVlMTEtODkyNS0wMDIyNDgyMjNmMzYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=F7IR7iyseFjDt3qtqbkD29fH1q-1pUxvJyq7OIoKDf8=) I’ve taken a lot of tough fights in my time — and it’s all been in the name of giving back. We have a saying as part of my Jewish faith — “Tikkun Olam,” or repairing the world. There’s a lot that’s been broken, and a lot to fix. I’m ready to do my part to leave our state and country in a better place, and to repair our broken democracy, but I can’t do it alone. **[With less than 100 days until Californians go to the polls, my team needs your help to share our message across California’s 58 counties and win this U.S. Senate race. clean_body: | Hi there, it’s Adam Schiff. Can I share a picture with you? = This is me at 13, in all my “glory” at my Bar Mitzvah. It’s easy to chuckle at this photo — and see just how far fashion has changed since that classic absolutely righteous 1970s bowtie — but it is also an opportunity to tell you about my upbringing. My family moved around while I was in school before settling in Danville, California. My parents and my teachers cultivated in me a love of and respect for public service. While in speech class, I remember listening to recordings of great speakers like President John F. Kennedy, the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr., and Winston Churchill. I admired the way they used language — how they could inspire millions of people to take action through the power of their words. I wanted to use words — and actions — in the service of progressive change. And I wanted to be part of the great struggle for the future. After graduating high school (I was not valedictorian as some have claimed — my B in Band held me back), I went on to college and law school. There, I learned how to gather the facts and argue my case. = After law school, I was inspired by friends serving in office and decided I was ready to try. I ran for the California Assembly. And, folks, I lost. It was bruising to lose, but I didn’t give up. And then, I lost again. But I refused to give up hope. I continued campaigning and rallying — and just two years later, I was elected to represent the 21st District in the State Senate. I was sworn in as the California Senate’s youngest member at just 36 years old. = After the term finished, I threw my hat in the ring to take on the Republican incumbent in California’s 27th congressional district. This was seen as one of the seats that could decide the House majority. Money poured into this election — the most expensive in history at the time. I barnstormed the district — speaking with voters to share our message. Those long months of hard work paid off: Despite the election of George W. Bush as president and Republicans maintaining their House majority, we flipped that seat and won that race, and I became only the second Democrat to represent the district in history. = I’ve taken a lot of tough fights in my time — and it’s all been in the name of giving back. We have a saying as part of my Jewish faith — “Tikkun Olam,” or repairing the world. There’s a lot that’s been broken, and a lot to fix. I’m ready to do my part to leave our state and country in a better place, and to repair our broken democracy, but I can’t do it alone. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation between Jason Crow and Adam Schiff will be processed immediately: | | = = | = = | = = Thank you, Adam = Jason Crow for Congress 8547 E Arapahoe Road, STE J-543 Greenwood Village, CO 80112 United States | mailto:info@jasoncrowforcongress.com | Paid for by Jason Crow for Congress Jason Crow was a Captain in the U.S. Army. Folks, No one wants to think about the worst case scenario of a second Trump presidency. But _The Atlantic_ just gave us a reality check. | **“If Donald Trump returns to the White House, he’d bring a better understanding of the system’s vulnerabilities, more willing enablers, and a more focused agenda of retaliation”**
_\- The Atlantic_
---

International vacations... high-end wine... five-star hotels... Michelin restaurants... an expensive athletic hobby, running races across the country and billing the hotels to her donors.
**Sinema’s pattern is clear:**
* Step 1: raises money from special interests (like private equity)
* Step 2: do legislative favors for those special interests (like protecting the carried interest loophole)
* Step 3: spend their money to subsidize a lavish lifestyle of luxury of five-star hotels and Michelin star restaurants and international jet setting
* Step 4: ignore constituents, and repeat

As one ethics expert said, “**It is one thing to ask donors for money to support your campaign and get your message out to voters, it is another to ask them to bankroll your personal life.** ”

name: Michael Bennet
subject: Boebert is letting down Colorado
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY BENNET FOR COLORADO
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/embutton?refcode=X_120823_Boebert_actrs [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/embutton?refcode=X_120823_Boebert_actrs]
Friend,
Once the steel capital of the West, Pueblo powered our state and our country for decades. But like many American cities, Pueblo paid the price for a 40-year Washington consensus that stretches back to Ronald Reagan.
It's easy to summarize: National Republicans cut taxes for the wealthiest Americans and corporations, which slashed investments in the American people, and companies shipped our supply chains and jobs overseas.
Americans have rejected this agenda, and we’ve begun to chart a new course.
We passed the Inflation Reduction Act – the most significant climate legislation that any country on the planet has ever passed.
Unfortunately, not every leader in Colorado supports this progress. Lauren Boebert voted against the Inflation Reduction Act — the law that’s bringing hundreds of good-paying jobs to her district.
Because of this bill, the United States is better positioned than any country in the world to lead the global transition to clean energy. And there is no state in America better positioned to lead the country in our transition than Colorado.
President Biden recently toured CS Wind in Colorado, the world's largest manufacturing plant for wind turbines, which plans to expand as a result of the Inflation Reduction Act. This expansion will create over 800 new good-paying jobs in Pueblo.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/embutton?refcode=X_120823_Boebert_actrs [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/embutton?refcode=X_120823_Boebert_actrs]

The IRA has been critical to my work building an economy that works for everybody, not just the people at the top. We’ve made big strides, but progress takes time. Will you support my fight to build a better future for Colorado by chipping in now? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/embutton?refcode=X_120823_Boebert_actrs]
Boebert's priorities are clear. Her commitment is to the corporate PACs and Republican donors lining her pockets, not her constituents.
Colorado deserves representatives who will help them build a better future. But, when Boebert had the opportunity to create good-paying, clean energy jobs in her district, she voted against it.
In 2024, we have an opportunity to elect a Democrat to Lauren Boebert’s seat — and take back control of the House in the process. Will you chip in now to help us unseat Lauren Boebert, elect Democrats, and make progress for Colorado? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/embutton?refcode=X_120823_Boebert_actrs]

body:
[ stdin# ][IMG]

Peter Willis,

The U.S. Constitution leaves wealth taxation to voters, not the courts. But in Moore v. United States, the Supreme Court threatens to change that.

The Court is hearing arguments right now from lawyers for the super-rich who want to stop Congress from ever considering a wealth tax. Whether it’s what the people want or not.

That’s not just bad public policy, it’s a betrayal of American democracy.

Sign if you agree: The wealthy must pay their fair share of taxes. (https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/12991?source=EM_NBI_OR_20231208_PT_roswap_0_6MO_ourrevolution_na_na_decroswap&t=1011&akid=4979%2E5885482%2ECjI2m7)

ADD YOUR NAME (https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/12991?source=EM_NBI_OR_20231208_PT_roswap_0_6MO_ourrevolution_na_na_decroswap&t=1012&akid=4979%2E5885482%2ECjI2m7)

According to the latest estimates, a tax on the ultra-rich can yield $3 trillion a year and provide critical funds for healthcare, child care, housing, education, and infrastructure. Yet corporate lobbyists are using their influence to prevent billionaires and multi-millionaires from paying their fair share.

We can’t let the ultra-rich dictate how much they pay in taxes, or whether they will pay taxes at all, while Americans struggle to make ends meet and wealth inequality continues to grow.

My name is Kevin Lincoln, and my story, is the Valley’s story. I am a 3rd generation Stocktonian, raising a 4th generation in the city I love. I’m the grandson of Mexican immigrants, and my stepfather is an Army veteran.

Like many Stocktonians, my family has overcome economic setbacks. My own father struggled to survive on these streets, and was at one time, homeless. But I never let adversity define me. I joined the Marines and served in the White House Military Office, assigned to Marine One. I graduated college while working full-time and raising a family. I’ve worked in corporate America and served our community as a pastor, and as a non-profit leader.

I’m blessed with a beautiful wife, Bonnie, and two amazing children. I’ve lived a life of service, but the greatest honor of my life has been giving back to my community, through serving as Mayor of my hometown, Stockton.

Fellow American,
---
My name is Pat Harrigan. You don’t know me, but I’m a Green Beret veteran from North Carolina. I graduated from West Point and fought in frontline combat for 18 months in some of the worst conditions on the planet. But I believe that my most important accomplishment is my family. I’m the dad of two beautiful girls and the husband of a loving wife. I’m a tried and true leader ready to take on my next great challenge: **I’m officially announcing my run for Congress in North Carolina.**
---
[**STAND WITH PAT HARRIGAN **](http://links.patharriganforcongress.com/u/click?_t=d400fe4f8ca24360a0914af7db39ca7b&_m=e815656d62c64dcd983779375a8a4131&_e=QgFX5ap2Hqu-eNK2btja5vbVcZURoxc-q_JmuaiifdO5X6RfPx0FQFWm1I9Ai0PHa580T0BqWuHLzwxuM-GaEjXkZL-R9BUJLvS1BtC5M0CtwqaIuXVNZf9lITd9qUD6PB5QrwQGNIZyJhw9jS0g0YxYBlBTnezruTnGCFjp-AwzCtRtwA5VJLORnsTORl6wHkqBgAKlzPhAxi8I7RfxNR7MJBMHrkhTTJ_ikmjtqENR2IPUMBnRQ66b5TP7Zhd_d33reU1sXDSBMhet-VCykFEvoeI6KkLxpg1GMVQqAbmbS3xYqp_BYTL2Mk-aaKPF4UzhTrE3CMC1deRShMbbU0SpYcU977Xf6jJsu2LwvKKLFnD__Rm6buDMxFYohFCOPUuZPg0GMCaJy5pv_pr1Tw%3D%3D)
---
When I came home from combat, I was shocked by how our so-called “leaders” in Washington were treating the American people. Instead of serving the people’s best interests - they have sold themselves out to a group of no-name bureaucrats fueled by greed. Even worse is the radical-Left’s destructive agenda designed to rip apart the societal fabric of America. As a father of girls, it frightens me to imagine the country they’ll be faced with when they’re my age. It doesn’t have to be this way, Fellow American. I’m one of the 10’s millions of American who knows this: our country officially hit **code-red.** We desperately need leadership that puts power BACK into the hands of The People, or we may be doomed. But just like during my time in the Green Berets, I need a top-tier team by my side to help me carry this fight all the way to Washington. **[I’m asking with humility - can I count on seeing your name on my list of founding Patriots ready to RETAKE DC?](http://links.patharriganforcongress.com/u/click?_t=d400fe4f8ca24360a0914af7db39ca7b&_m=e815656d62c64dcd983779375a8a4131&_e=QgFX5ap2Hqu-eNK2btja5vbVcZURoxc-q_JmuaiifdO5X6RfPx0FQFWm1I9Ai0PHa580T0BqWuHLzwxuM-GaEjXkZL-R9BUJLvS1BtC5M0CtwqaIuXVNZf9lITd9qUD6PB5QrwQGNIZyJhw9jS0g0YxYBlBTnezruTnGCFjp-AwzCtRtwA5VJLORnsTORl6wHkqBgAKlzPhAxi8I7RfxNR7MJBMHrkhTTJ_ikmjtqENR2IPUMBnRQ66b5TP7Zhd_821zvhSBQ1Lmm1PhI9hsn0AxqUiPRJ4j5F1Vbh-WhiZgE_7ZX0dlOCInE-T12dKlKXQby5PqK1YNNbmC041zAwnDEAO06010iISvkWWNvW7iOsBwtzZ27xmu488dTcil4g2pSD1j7WfHt9xug9DjHw%3D%3D)**

A plan to finally ensure billionaires pay their fair share, just like the rest of us.** A hard-working teacher or firefighter in Philomath, Oregon, doesn't get to call up an army of high-priced lawyers and accountants whenever they don't feel like paying their taxes. Working families pay taxes out of each paycheck, but the same rules don't apply to billionaires. Friend,
**Reports indicate I will once again take the WITNESS STAND for the fake trial in New York on Monday.**
Not since Teddy Roosevelt – over 100 years ago – has a former U.S. President taken the witness stand.
Teddy was defending himself from what he called an **“alliance of corruption”** between the political machines that had seized control of both the Republicans and the Democrats.
_...Sound familiar, Friend?_
Much like Teddy, I am a relentless fighter and a “happy warrior” in our mission to buck the political machine and put the _American people_ first.

| | Dear Peter, Yesterday, I received a push notification on my phone with this headline. Well, here was my answer. **Throughout history, minority communities have been the target of bigotry, oppression, and hatred for their existence. The fear of violence and persecution would be so great that any celebration or expression of their culture was viewed as a risk.** This pain and fear is known well in the Jewish community, but can also be found in Black and brown communities, Asian communities, and among our LGBTQ+ brothers and sisters. **I'm committed to fighting on behalf of these communities, not just for their rights to exist, but so they can thrive and celebrate in a world that isn't defined by hate.** That's why I march in Pride parades. That's why I speak at rallies against Asian Hate. That's why I stand up for Black lives. And that's why I put a menorah in the window last night. My wish for this holiday season is that the forces of light — both in our menorahs and in our politics — prevail over darkness. And as I was lighting the first candle last night, and thinking of the miracle of Hanukkah, I was reminded of a question about the holiday. Most of us know the story of how the Maccabees only had enough oil to light the lamps for one night, but it lasted for eight nights. A question arose of why it is not a seven-day holiday; after all, they knew they had enough oil for one night so why don't we just celebrate the next seven as the miracle? The answer is that there _was_ a miracle on that first night: **it was the courage to light the menorah without knowing how long it would last — the courage to take the first step without knowing where your second one may be.** I want to thank you all for standing alongside me in this campaign, in what has been a trying time for many. Our movement is a first step towards building a world lifted up by love and respect, not hate — and hopefully won't be the last. More soon, _Nick_ |

subject: Do you know these Pennsylvania fun facts?

body:
# [](https://go.bobcasey.com/go/181?t=1&akid=1331%2E552475%2EkEMvRc)
Peter, fun fact: you probably know that the Declaration of Independence was signed in Philadelphia in 1776, but did you also know that Philly was the capital of the United States from 1790 to 1800?
I’m one of our Commonwealth’s number one fans, so there’s a lot more where that came from.
Before I share, my Finance Director, Taylor, said that I can’t use this email to only recite facts about Pennsylvania, no matter how much I might want to. I should also ask folks to chip in to help me continue representing the place I’ve always called home.
**[Peter, will you chip in now to help me continue fighting for my fellow Pennsylvanians in the U.S. Senate?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/casey-em-20231208-3?refcode=em20231208-3&refcode2=1331_552475_kEMvRc&akid=1331%2E552475%2EkEMvRc) **
Now that’s out of the way, are you ready for some more facts?
Did you know that Pennsylvania’s Fayette County is home to Fort Necessity, where George Washington experienced his first military combat in 1754?
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/casey-em-20231208-3?refcode=em20231208-3&refcode2=1331_552475_kEMvRc&akid=1331%2E552475%2EkEMvRc)
Or that William Maclay — a member of Pennsylvania’s first United States Senate delegation — kept a diary during his term, which became one of few historical accounts of the 1st United States Congress?
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/casey-em-20231208-3?refcode=em20231208-3&refcode2=1331_552475_kEMvRc&akid=1331%2E552475%2EkEMvRc)
Or here’s a fun one: the world’s first computer was built in Philadelphia in 1946!
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/casey-em-20231208-3?refcode=em20231208-3&refcode2=1331_552475_kEMvRc&akid=1331%2E552475%2EkEMvRc)
These are just a few of my favorite pieces of Pennsylvania trivia, Peter. I love the Commonwealth and its history. Just recently, my team challenged me to name all 67 of our counties — and I did it in under 10 minutes.
[**Now I’m hoping you’ll chip in $10 or more to support our re-election fight. I’m Pennsylvania through and through, and I need your support to keep making progress for our Commonwealth.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/casey-em-20231208-3?refcode=em20231208-3&refcode2=1331_552475_kEMvRc&akid=1331%2E552475%2EkEMvRc)

Hi, Peter. Ted Cruz here. _Far too many_ career politicians in D.C. are desperate to cling onto their power by any means necessary. And left unchecked, they hold their power for **DECADES!__[THIS IS WRONG>>](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/u/click?_t=5b1853ae48754bee8f471363fe4933a9&_m=2d57807cd01743a283beaf6c49144671&_e=bODFEW-MK_A7F2TVhp6vTkYHrPTxwpxR0xDI3NPuG9-wrez0kqcXHK02p7A3AP5pjNdq8lqaxB7nDqry8FRl4ashCk3HWwMVats2A3JeGiUi2A-AMrK8iNJrCmVleDo9WctqXJqwI9MiE8-EInHIHAGIvIsX4-Obf4p5OmmGFebC4Eo1_H_ui1mimvM5biLUGggMaid--S2m0QUmYbDHo4FBzlcYoybmwv7aNgFoLFNJmdlXG8FKX4joJ7yTWb5Zw7-7GY-0vxjPbSTIKX706OP9_KmhQRyZTtcRnLBUhoAWiKXBQgickzEvspgWAUIISymlpfrDkK1D3iF88xV7cjewR_bJb08g-J7V_HlXBUba2gS0jyu1JcKnVlawUyEE)__** That’s why I am sponsoring legislation to _**[add a Term Limits Amendment to the U.S. Constitution](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/u/click?_t=5b1853ae48754bee8f471363fe4933a9&_m=2d57807cd01743a283beaf6c49144671&_e=bODFEW-MK_A7F2TVhp6vTkYHrPTxwpxR0xDI3NPuG9-wrez0kqcXHK02p7A3AP5pjNdq8lqaxB7nDqry8FRl4ashCk3HWwMVats2A3JeGiUi2A-AMrK8iNJrCmVleDo9WctqXJqwI9MiE8-EInHIHAGIvIsX4-Obf4p5OmmGFebC4Eo1_H_ui1mimvM5biLUGggMaid--S2m0QUmYbDHo4FBzlcYoybmwv7aNgFoLFMIyobt5DVDBoqiGmDQlJIp6hG1I8p4hm9cTbmw24SqQrU0S6aZ4cBj80ZX0QyTlBjofGUtA5NpIxMtn2eJRj47O258u0CrsT98ByWDcITw0kEifGfZbEsNHhpEaWFwffskHvUNlHoWDcQCku6mtyOw)**_ and why I am hopeful you will support this effort with your own voice today. Under my Term Limits Amendment, lawmakers in D.C. would:

subject: To me, policy is personal
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
Did you know that over half of all Members of Congress are millionaires? Meanwhile, the median household income is only $70,784. 👈🏽 **This is wild.**
Many of our lawmakers have no lived experience of working paycheck to paycheck or trying to pay rent working a low-wage job.
To me, policy is personal. When I worked as a bartender, I relied on tips to pay the bills. I know the urgent and daily stresses of working class people because I have lived them. And I intimately understand how important measures like raising the minimum wage, universal health care, universal child care, and free college can be for families living in financial uncertainty.
That’s why I’m in Congress: **to represent working families like mine.**
I am honored to be here, and I can’t do this work without you — the grassroots supporters who have had my back every step of the way. I can’t self-fund my campaign by writing a big check, and I don’t do any donor call-time or exclusive fundraising events.

subject: Legislative Session Update
body:
Official Newsletter

WEEKLY UPDATE FROM REP. RYAN CHAMBERLIN
District 24,

Thank you for reading this weekly update! I had a busy week in Tallahassee, meeting with my fellow legislators for committee meetings and talking to constituents and stakeholders about their legislative priorities. I look forward to keeping you updated on my work in the Florida House.

As always, if there is an issue you would like me to address in Tallahassee, please contact me. It would be a pleasure to meet with you! I want to ensure our district and state stay strong for the next generation of Floridians.
Florida Beer Wholesalers Association dinner with Tri-County Distribution
Over the weekend, I had the honor of attending a dinner for the Florida Beer Wholesalers Association with Tri-County Distribution. It was a pleasure to meet with representatives from this organization who are working hard to educate policymakers and the public about the value of regulating and manufacturing the distribution and sale of alcoholic beverages in Florida.
Meeting with Chancellor Ray Rodrigues of the State University System of Florida
On Monday, I had the wonderful opportunity to meet with Chancellor Ray Rodrigues of the State University System of Florida. We had a productive time discussing legislative priorities for the upcoming legislative session. We talked about multiple topics pertaining to higher education and how the university system is structured.
Meetings with constituents and organizations
On Tuesday, I had several meetings with constituents and organizations.

That morning I had a meeting with Tom Chase, CEO of Langley Health Services, and the Florida Association of Community Health Centers to discuss legislative priorities and appropriations requests going into the 2024 Legislative Session.

------------------------------------------------------------

Then, I moved on to a meeting with members of the Bleeding Disorders Coalition of Florida to discuss HB 363 (https://www.myfloridahouse.gov/Sections/Bills/billsdetail.aspx?BillId=78959&utm_source=Ryan+Chamberlin+for+State+Representative&utm_campaign=7ddd94a0de-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_12_08_05_14&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-7ddd94a0de-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D) , a piece of legislation that would protect health plan consumers from discriminatory copay accumulator adjuster programs. This bill was seen in the Select Committee for Health Innovation, which I have the honor of sitting on.

------------------------------------------------------------

Later in the morning on Tuesday, I had the chance to speak with Henry Fortier, Superintendent of Catholic Schools of the Diocese of Orlando. We discussed a variety of legislative issues, such as federal program issues, scholarship program fixes, school choice, and safety and security.

------------------------------------------------------------

After lunch, I had the pleasure to meet with and hear Marion County constituent Kylie Hurst who spoke to the Senate on 4H and its impact on her veterinary career. Kylie shared her story of how 4H helped her develop her veterinary skills and helped her gain the confidence to pursue a career in veterinary medicine. She was a great example of how 4H can be a platform for young people to explore and develop their interests. I'm inspired by Kylie's story, and I'm grateful for her taking the time to share it with us.

------------------------------------------------------------

Afterward, I attended a meeting with members of the Florida Auto Dismantlers and Recyclers Association to discuss issues that have been happening around the state and to also share how bills from previous legislative sessions have impacted them.

------------------------------------------------------------

Later in the afternoon, I met with the staff of Florida Cares Charity, a non-profit dedicated to improving the lives of the incarcerated. They briefed me on how their organization is making a difference in the lives of Floridians and made appropriations requests for the upcoming session.

------------------------------------------------------------

Finally, on Tuesday, I met with members of the American Institute of Architects Florida Chapter to discuss legislative priorities affecting those in their industry. We discussed the importance of passing legislation to protect architects and their industry from unfair regulations and fees. We also discussed the importance of passing legislation to ensure that architects and their industry are given the same support as other professional industries.
Wednesday was another busy day in Tallahassee, with numerous meetings with constituents and organizations. I also had a committee to attend.

On Wednesday morning, I met with constituents from around the state to discuss voter integrity in our elections, along with upcoming bills that may be seen in the upcoming Legislative Session.

------------------------------------------------------------

Afterward, I met with members of the Florida Association of Postsecondary Schools and Colleges to discuss their legislative priorities and share the positive impact the schools are making on Florida’s workforce, including healthcare.

------------------------------------------------------------
Finally, that afternoon, I met with a team from the Florida Association of Professional Geologists during the Groups Day at the Capitol Lobbying Day Event, and we discussed Geological issues in the State of Florida and potential solutions for them.

------------------------------------------------------------
Friends, as you can see, it was a busy week in Tallahassee serving our District and interests. I am honored to serve you as your State Representative. If I may be of any assistance, please do not hesitate to contact my office by clicking here (https://www.myfloridahouse.gov/Sections/Representatives/contactmember.aspx?MemberId=4901&SessionId=103&utm_source=Ryan+Chamberlin+for+State+Representative&utm_campaign=7ddd94a0de-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_12_08_05_14&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-7ddd94a0de-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D) .

I wish you all a very Happy Holiday Season!

Best regards,

Ryan Chamberlin
State Representative
District 24

| Dear Friend,
As a passionate champion of conservative values and a dedicated servant to the citizens of New Hampshire, I am immensely proud to have secured the endorsement of the 603 Alliance. Over more than a decade of legislative service, I have remained steadfast in delivering concrete outcomes for New Hampshire families. My record as a Granite State conservative speaks for itself, boasting substantial tax reductions, staunch defense of our constitutional rights, and an unyielding dedication to advancing the principles of limited government. I am proud that the 603 Alliance recognizes that record and will be supporting my campaign to take that record to Concord.
Check out their official endorsement bellow!

---
---
| | |
---
| |
---
| |
---
_Morse stands alone as the sole candidate with a tangible record of defending our 2nd Amendment rights, reducing taxes for small businesses and homeowners, vehemently opposing amnesty for illegal immigrants, advocating for education freedom, and prioritizing an America-first energy policy._

_Morse has a proven record of substantive accomplishments that he consistently delivered while in the NH Senate. Ayotte's rhetoric on the campaign trail may mimic conservative ideals, but her actions during her one term in the United States Senate often retreated from these principles.
_ _As a border state, it is critical that our NH Governor take a firm stand against illegal immigration. While in the United States Senate, Kelly Ayotte voted for the "Gang of Eight" immigration reform bill that would have given citizenship to the people who entered the United States illegally._ _Having served with Chuck Morse in the NH legislature, Fran Wendleboe states, "There is not anyone better qualified and prepared to be Governor than Chuck Morse. His actions and accomplishments reflect the qualities of a genuine conservative leader. In addition, Morse's track record, for over a decade, was dedicated to delivering concrete results for Granite State families, which instills our trust that he will seamlessly continue this successful legacy from day one."_

We need leaders in Washington who will lead on gun violence prevention because this is not a partisan issue but rather a matter of protecting our communities. We can no longer wait.

| Peter,

This week marks the 30th anniversary of the mass shooting on the Long Island Rail Road commuter train, which killed 6 people and injured 19. Among those who were killed was former Rep. Carolyn McCarthy's husband and her son, who was injured.

Over the years, gun violence has devastated the lives of thousands of Americans. And I know this is true: Americans are united in that we need to put an end to senseless gun violence. I’m proud to be endorsed by Rep. Carolyn McCarthy, who, throughout her career, fought for gun reform on Capitol Hill.

We need leaders in Washington who will lead on gun violence prevention because this is not a partisan issue but rather a matter of protecting our communities. _**We can no longer wait.**_

I will fight for gun reform in Congress starting DAY ONE because nothing is more important to me than the safety of our communities today and in the future.

Thank you,

Laura Gillen

Derek — I had the opportunity to speak with a retired longshoreman a few months back, and I just had to share his story.
I asked him how he was doing in his retirement.
And he said, “When I was a longshoreman, I didn’t go to the doctor unless I was bleeding...Now that I’m retired, I go all the damn time. **And this union gave me health care.”**
**That’s what labor does for people. It gives them a chance to be paid fairly and retire with dignity.**
Day after day on the campaign trail, I hear incredible stories from hard-working people who are concerned about whether their pay and benefits will be enough to support themselves and their families.
The reality is that our economy is not working for far too many people.
And the problem isn’t that people aren’t working. **It’s that people are working and still can’t make enough to get by.**
That’s why this longshoreman’s story has stuck with me. The power of collective bargaining through a union has paved the way for workers to get better wages and benefits, safer working conditions, and a dignified retirement.
From the start of my career, I’ve stood shoulder to shoulder with the labor movement. I launched this campaign at the IATSE Hall — the home of the labor union that powers our film and television industry. I’ve marched on picket lines with striking writers and actors, and I’ve introduced legislation to give them access to the unemployment benefits they depend on while they’re fighting for all of us.
**I’m going to keep fighting to protect workers, like the retired longshoreman I met on the campaign trail. From the writers and actors to autoworkers and Amazon factory workers, the labor movement is driving progress toward making the economy work for everyone, and in the Senate, I will never stop fighting for working people.**
**[If you support my fight to pass legislation empowering our workers, securing fair and equitable working conditions, and creating good-paying union jobs, please contribute to my campaign for U.S. Senate today.
